name: Amadeus on AI: trust governance, agentic standards and the AI Foundry
title: Amadeus on AI: trust governance, agentic standards and the AI Foundry
answer: Amadeus, the travel technology and distribution company, publishes an AI Trust Center, blog articles and a glossary covering how it governs and deploys AI across travel. Its most useful single point for hospitality readers is that agentic AI needs more than the Model Context Protocol: the company's chief technology officer argues travel retailing also requires commerce protocols, a neutral execution layer, integrated business logic and a trusted system of record before conversational agents can complete real bookings. That frames where hotel distribution sits as AI agents begin to shop and book.

sections.body: Amadeus, the travel technology company behind a global distribution system, publishes this material on amadeus.com. The pages read include the AI Trust Center, a governance page setting out its AI Policy, AI Office and AI Trust Board, blog articles on the AI Foundry, agentic AI standards, airline adoption and corporate travel, and a travel glossary entry defining artificial intelligence. The material dates from 2026, with one article recapping the first half of 2026. It is company published and promotional in tone, but substantive about products, positions and governance.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: Amadeus describes itself as the embedded and neutral execution layer for travel, connecting suppliers, sellers and AI players. Its AI Trust Center sets out an AI Policy covering ethical, secure and legally compliant use of AI worldwide, structured to meet obligations under the EU AI Act and other regulations, with an AI Office and a cross functional AI Trust Board. Principles listed include fairness and human oversight, reliability and safety, privacy and data security, explainability and transparency, human control and environmental sustainability. Amadeus is a signatory of the European Commission's AI Pact. The AI Foundry, part of the AI Delivery Hub, turns common AI challenges into reusable capabilities across the portfolio, and Amadeus Max, an AI assistant layer, has shown a 76% reduction in handling time in travel seller workflows. On agentic AI, chief technology officer Sylvain Roy argues that Model Context Protocol adoption is a first step but insufficient for complex retailing, and that emerging commerce protocols such as Universal Commerce Protocol could enable end to end transactions. Travelers increasingly trust AI to research trips and may soon let agents transact for them, expecting multi modal conversation and end to end journey management. Airlines are advised to start with a few high return workflows such as call centre automation, and to prepare data, APIs and industry semantics. Amadeus cites a data mesh governing 30 petabytes of travel data.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: Amadeus says Amadeus Max has shown a 76% reduction in handling time across key workflows in travel seller environments, and that AI agent productivity tools in the back office reduced customer handling times by 76% on average in the travel industry. It says its data mesh normalizes and governs 30 petabytes of high quality travel data. It says the whitepaper 'Airlines in the agentic age' proposes five practical recommendations. It notes that Model Context Protocol was originally launched by Anthropic and is now supported by Microsoft, Google and OpenAI. It says it acquired SkyLink, an AI first, New York headquartered technology company specializing in orchestration and conversational automation, and names Sylvain Roy as Chief Technology Officer.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in hospitality would use this source to understand how the distribution layer beneath hotel and airline booking is being rebuilt for AI agents. Amadeus's argument that Model Context Protocol alone cannot handle complex retailing, and that a neutral execution layer with integrated business logic and a trusted system of record is needed, speaks directly to how hotel inventory and offers are personalized and transacted when agents act on a traveler's behalf. The governance material shows how a major distribution system is approaching EU AI Act compliance, while the AI Foundry and Amadeus Max give a concrete sense of where operational AI is being applied in seller environments.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Hospitality

sections.body: The material is company published and largely promotional, with few independent figures and no methodology behind the 76% claims. Most examples concern airlines, corporate travel and travel sellers rather than hotels specifically, so hotel level detail is thin. Dates are given only for some items, notably the first half of 2026 recap. The glossary entry is introductory rather than analytical, and the pages describe Amadeus products and positions rather than offering neutral assessment.
